title: Manager Who Builds Worlds
description:
I got fired for sleeping at work. Fair.

What wasn't fair was the glowing orb waiting outside my apartment when I got home.

【You have been selected as a Constellation Manager.】

"Selected by who?"

【Permission level insufficient.】

No answers. Just a dead planet and a system shop that sells everything from grass seed to rain clouds, and a job: rebuild a civilization from nothing.

The system calls it a sacred responsibility. I call it unpaid labor.

Rent is due in fourteen days. If this world can't make me money, I'm not interested. If it can, I'll build it up and squeeze it for everything it's worth.

title: Marked by False Gods
description:
Rule one: panic is a waste of oxygen.

I was mid-shift at the restaurant, customers arguing over nothing, when the room around us vanished and something else took its place. People screamed. I stayed quiet.

【Greetings, Human! Welcome to the Tutorial!】

The world had turned into a staged game with rules, timers, and something watching from the other side. I'm not the strongest person here. I don't need to be. I just need to see what everyone else misses, and every situation has a pressure point.

Whatever is running this calls itself a god. I don't buy it. Gods don't need games.

"Life is an adventure, I guess."

Stay alive long enough to learn the rules. After that, I start playing for real.

title: Masquerade in Noble Court
description:
"I know this story," I told the ceiling. "Mostly."

I woke up as Elena, a count's daughter the novel had already decided to throw away. No magic, no position worth remembering, five months before the family title lapsed and the story stopped needing her at all.

The survival plan was simple. Ignore the Crown Prince, ignore the heroine, don't die.

So I went to the imperial temple for a mana retest. It should have been a formality.

【Water Affinity Confirmed.】

The priest stopped mid-sentence.

I looked at the crystal again. It still said the same thing.

This wasn't in the book.

"Well. That's inconvenient."

title: Mistakenly Dragged Survival
description:
[System Error: Player "Jiang Wenxu" assigned to incorrect entry position.]

A borrowed umbrella and a swapped name tag, and Jiang Wenxu got pulled into the Nightmare Game in a stranger's place. The system dropped him straight into an S-Rank instance.

[Survival Probability: NULL.]

He cleared it on the first try.

The spectator feed went quiet for half a second, then detonated.

"A newbie cleared S-Rank? Is he a retired god?"

"His heart rate didn't even flicker. He's a monster."

Jiang Wenxu had just done the correct thing at each step, without hesitating. By the time the system logged the result, the instance was already over.

[Instance Clear. Performance: ANOMALOUS.]

title: Monarch of Depravity
description:
Log Entry 01: "What a shitty transmigration."

I woke up in a body its last owner had already abandoned, in a room set up for a ritual sacrifice. The original soul is gone. If no offering is made before dawn, the body goes with it.

I don't know why I'm here, or why I landed in a situation built on rules nobody gave me. What I do know is that the system running all of this is weirdly consistent, and the gaps in it feel deliberate.

The ritual needs a life before sunrise. The body I'm wearing qualifies, unless I find something else first.

"I have no words," I said. "I'm screwed."

title: Mutation of the Apocalypse
description:
Year 0, Day 1: "Auditory hallucination," Lucas decided, and blew out his birthday candle.

【INITIATING EARTH MUTATION PROGRAM: PHASE 1】

By morning the world had changed, and his neighbor was trying to break down his door to kill him.

Lucas didn't panic. He had worked since he was a kid, and panic never changed an outcome yet. He handled the neighbor. By afternoon he had killed enough to trigger a reward notification, so he collected the drops, logged them, and kept moving. There were places to reach and supplies didn't wait.

"So it starts," he muttered. "Fine."
